system:
You are the city manager of a simulated city in crisis. Your job is to get the city healthy again within a limited number of turns by adjusting policy levers.

You cannot see the city. Everything you know about it must come from SQL queries against its data warehouse, which records one row per entity per simulated month for the city's entire history. Query it. The history before your first turn shows how the city got into this state, and is usually the fastest route to the cause.

Each turn you may issue several `sql_query` calls, then call `set_levers` with the changes you want. Levers persist between turns, so you only need to set what you are changing. Advancing to the next turn happens automatically once you commit.

Work like an analyst: find what is actually failing before you spend money on it. The city's budget is finite, and a lever set far past what the problem needs will cost more than it repairs. When you have decided, call `set_levers` and briefly say why.

## Data catalog

This warehouse is catalogued in DataHub, a metadata platform that records what each table and column means, defines the business terms behind them, and tracks which tables are derived from which. That documentation is reproduced in full below -- it is everything the catalog holds about this warehouse, so there is nothing further to look up.

Use it to skip discovery. You do not need to inspect information_schema or sample tables to work out what a column holds; it is described here. Lineage is generated from the simulation's own causal graph and every edge is verified against the running model, so 'derived from' states a real causal dependency rather than a guess -- it tells you which inputs actually move a given output.

### sim_run
One simulation invocation: seed, horizon, grid size, wall-clock bounds.
Columns:
  - run_id: Surrogate key for the run.
  - seed: RNG seed that fully determines the city.
  - years: Simulated years requested.
  - grid_w: Map width in tiles.
  - grid_h: Map height in tiles.
  - started_at: Wall-clock start.
  - finished_at: Wall-clock finish, null while running.
### ticks
Simulated calendar: each row is one month of city time for a run.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Months elapsed from start (0 = initial snapshot).
  - year: 1-based simulated year.
  - month: 1-based month within the year.
### tiles
Spatial grid cells: terrain and zoning. The map the viewer draws.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tile_id: Stable tile id (row-major).
  - x: Grid column.
  - y: Grid row.
  - terrain: grass | water | rock.
  - zoning: none | residential | commercial | industrial | mixed.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.zoning_release -> tiles.zoning
### tile_monthly
Per-tile condition each month: abandonment, utility load, power service.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - tile_id: Tile.
  - condition: 0 new … 1 ruined appearance.
  - abandonment: 0 occupied … 1 abandoned lot.
  - power_served: Whether the tile has power this month.
  - water_load: Local water load proxy.
  - sewer_load: Local sewer load proxy.
### buildings
Structures placed on tiles: type, capacity, assessed value.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - building_id: Stable building id.
  - tile_id: Tile the building occupies.
  - building_type: residential | commercial | industrial | civic.
  - capacity: Occupancy or job capacity.
  - assessed_value: Tax assessment base.
Derived from: tiles
  tiles.zoning -> buildings.building_id
### building_monthly
Building condition and service each month — what the viewer shades.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - building_id: Building.
  - condition_band: new | worn | derelict.
  - condition_score: 0 new … 1 derelict.
  - occupancy: Current occupants or workers.
  - power_served: Electrified this month.
  - power_demand_kw: Electrical demand.
  - water_demand: Water demand units.
Derived from: power_monthly
  power_monthly.outage_fraction -> building_monthly.power_served
### households
Households located at a home tile and building.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - household_id: Stable household id.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile.
  - home_building_id: Home building.
### citizens
Individual people belonging to households.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - citizen_id: Stable citizen id.
  - household_id: Household membership.
### citizen_monthly
Jobs, income, satisfaction, and map position each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - citizen_id: Citizen.
  - household_id: Household.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile this month.
  - workplace_tile_id: Workplace tile.
  - job_sector: Employment sector.
  - income: Annual gross income.
  - disposable_income: Monthly income after tax and bills.
  - satisfaction: 0–1 well-being score.
  - pos_x: Map x position.
  - pos_y: Map y position.
  - employed: Employment flag.
  - uses_transit: Commute mode includes transit.
Derived from: building_monthly, commute_monthly, lever_monthly, migration_monthly, water_monthly
  building_monthly.power_served -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  citizen_monthly.disposable_income -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  commute_monthly.travel_time -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.electricity_tariff -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.income_tax_rate -> citizen_monthly.disposable_income
  lever_monthly.property_tax_rate -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.transit_fare -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  migration_monthly.net -> citizen_monthly.citizen_id
  water_monthly.load_ratio -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
### road_segments
Road network edges on the grid.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - segment_id: Stable segment id.
  - from_tile_id: Start tile.
  - to_tile_id: End tile.
  - from_x: Start x.
  - from_y: Start y.
  - to_x: End x.
  - to_y: End y.
### road_monthly
Traffic, wear, and congestion per segment per month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - segment_id: Road segment.
  - traffic: Traffic volume.
  - wear: 0 smooth … 1 ruined pavement.
  - congestion: 0 free-flow … 1 jammed.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.road_maintenance_budget -> road_monthly.wear
  road_monthly.wear -> road_monthly.congestion
### commute_monthly
Home↔work commute outcomes for each citizen each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - citizen_id: Citizen.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile.
  - workplace_tile_id: Workplace tile.
  - travel_time: Commute duration units.
  - uses_transit: Transit rider flag.
Derived from: road_monthly
  road_monthly.congestion -> commute_monthly.travel_time
### budget_monthly
Municipal revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - income_tax_revenue: Income tax collected.
  - property_tax_revenue: Property tax collected.
  - utility_revenue: Electricity bill revenue.
  - transit_revenue: Transit fare revenue.
  - road_spend: Road maintenance spend.
  - water_sewer_spend: Water/sewer capital spend.
  - other_spend: Other municipal spend.
  - balance: Revenue minus spend.
  - debt: Outstanding debt.
  - treasury: Cash on hand.
Derived from: citizen_monthly, lever_monthly
  budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue -> budget_monthly.balance
  budget_monthly.property_tax_revenue -> budget_monthly.balance
  citizen_monthly.citizen_id -> budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue
  citizen_monthly.income -> budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue
  lever_monthly.electricity_tariff -> budget_monthly.utility_revenue
  lever_monthly.income_tax_rate -> budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue
  lever_monthly.property_tax_rate -> budget_monthly.property_tax_revenue
  lever_monthly.road_maintenance_budget -> budget_monthly.road_spend
  lever_monthly.transit_fare -> budget_monthly.transit_revenue
  lever_monthly.water_sewer_capex -> budget_monthly.water_sewer_spend
### lever_monthly
Player lever positions in force each month (policy inputs).
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - income_tax_rate: Fraction tax on income.
  - property_tax_rate: Annual fraction of assessed value.
  - electricity_tariff: Retail currency per kWh.
  - road_maintenance_budget: Annual road spend.
  - water_sewer_capex: Annual water/sewer capital.
  - transit_fare: Fare per ride.
  - zoning_release: Share of land opened.
  - power_contract_mode: 0 spot, 1 fixed, 2 hedged.
### power_monthly
City-wide electricity demand, supply, outages, contract, tariff.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - demand_kw: Aggregate demand.
  - supply_kw: Available supply.
  - outage_fraction: Share of demand unserved.
  - contract_mode: spot | fixed | hedged.
  - tariff: Retail tariff in force.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.power_contract_mode -> power_monthly.outage_fraction
### water_monthly
Water and sewer capacity, demand, load ratio, failure rate.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - capacity: System capacity units.
  - demand: System demand units.
  - load_ratio: demand / capacity.
  - failure_rate: Stress-driven failure proxy.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.water_sewer_capex -> water_monthly.capacity
  water_monthly.capacity -> water_monthly.load_ratio
### migration_monthly
Household arrivals and departures, net migration, population.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - arrivals: People arriving.
  - departures: People leaving.
  - net: arrivals − departures.
  - population: Population after migration.
Derived from: citizen_monthly
  citizen_monthly.satisfaction -> migration_monthly.net

### Glossary
  - Building condition: Visible state band: new, worn, or derelict.
  - Citizen satisfaction: 0–1 well-being of a resident; drives migration.
  - Commute: Home-to-work travel along the road network.
  - Congestion: Traffic load relative to wear-adjusted capacity (0–1).
  - Disposable income: Monthly income remaining after tax and utility/transit bills.
  - Electricity tariff: Retail price charged per kilowatt-hour.
  - Income tax rate: Municipal fraction levied on household gross income.
  - Income tax revenue: Tax collected from household incomes in a month.
  - Migration: Households arriving or leaving in response to city conditions.
  - Municipal budget: City revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury.
  - Power contract mode: Procurement mode: spot, fixed, or hedged.
  - Power outage fraction: Share of electrical demand left unserved.
  - Property tax rate: Annual fraction of building assessed value collected as tax.
  - Road maintenance budget: Annual spend allocated to road repair.
  - Road wear: Pavement degradation on a network segment (0–1).
  - Tile zoning: Land-use designation controlling what may be built.
  - Transit fare: Price charged per transit ride.
  - Water and sewer capex: Annual capital investment in water and sewer capacity.
  - Water load ratio: Water/sewer demand divided by capacity.
  - Zoning release: Share of undeveloped land opened for development.

history.text:
Turn 1. You have 12 turns left, including this one.

Levers currently in force:
  income_tax_rate: 0.04
  property_tax_rate: 0.004
  electricity_tariff: 0.65
  road_maintenance_budget: 0
  water_sewer_capex: 0
  transit_fare: 8
  zoning_release: 0
  power_contract_mode: 0

DataHub assertions. The catalog documents the operating envelope a well-run city holds to, authored against this warehouse. Readings outside it are flagged, and each lever carries how much moving it is actually worth.

CITY STATE, outside documented range (3):
  road_monthly.wear = 0.969 -- above the documented maximum of 0.15. a maintained network settles near 0.06; sustained values near 1.0 mean no repair is reaching the roads
  water_monthly.load_ratio = 0.852 -- above the documented maximum of 0.8. demand over installed capacity; above 1.0 the system is serving more than it can supply and failures follow
  citizen_monthly.satisfaction = 0.568 -- below the documented minimum of 0.7. a well-run city sustains about 0.73; below 0.45 residents leave faster than they arrive

LEVERS, outside documented range (6 of 8):
  income_tax_rate = 0.04 -- below the documented range 0.1-0.14 [critical]. the only revenue lever that pays for itself. It raises about $12.2M a month per unit of rate and costs 0.5 of satisfaction per unit -- roughly $24M of revenue for every point of satisfaction given up, nine times better than property tax and a thousand times better than the electricity tariff. Around 0.065 covers operating spend at a healthy maintenance budget; about 0.096 also clears the inherited debt and builds six months of reserve inside the horizon. Past 0.14 the lost residents cost more than the rate raises
  water_sewer_capex = 0 -- below the documented range 5.6e+06-7.2e+06 [critical]. capacity moves by (annual capex / 12) / 6000 units a month against a decay of about 0.6, so roughly $43k a year merely holds capacity level and anything less shrinks it. Demand is near 2,100 against a post-shock capacity near 860: reaching a safe load ratio inside the horizon needs about $3.6M a year at the very least, and this band gets there with time left for the recovery to compound
  road_maintenance_budget = 0 -- below the documented range 3.2e+06-7.2e+06 [critical]. repair is proportional to existing wear, so wear settles at an equilibrium rather than hitting a floor: wear stabilises at roughly 0.0165 / ((budget/$1M) x 0.05). That puts $2.2M a year at wear 0.15, $3.3M at 0.10 and $5.5M at 0.06. Below about $2.2M the network never comes back inside its healthy range; above this band the extra spend buys very little and the treasury pays for it
  electricity_tariff = 0.65 -- above the documented range 0-0.1 [moderate]. the worst revenue lever in the city and the easiest to mistake for a good one. Each unit of tariff raises about $3,600 a month while taking $194,000 out of residents' disposable income -- it destroys 53 times what it collects, before the direct satisfaction penalty. Treat it as a price to keep low, never as a way to fund the recovery
  transit_fare = 8 -- above the documented range 0-2 [moderate]. a pure transfer: it collects exactly what it removes from riders' disposable income, about $22,000 a month per unit of fare in each direction, and the satisfaction penalty on the third of citizens who ride is unrecovered. There is no funding case for raising it; the cheapest fare is the best one
  power_contract_mode = 0 -- below the documented range 2-2 [low]. hedged is the best of the three but worth only about 1.4% overall. Supply is structurally short of demand and no contract mode closes that, so set it to hedged once and stop spending turns on power

RESPONSE TIMES -- how long each system takes to reflect a change:
  water_monthly.capacity: the slowest system in the city, and the only one that grows linearly rather than converging: capacity moves a fixed number of units a month, so the deficit closes on a schedule that cannot be made up later. Closing it takes about 36 months at $3.6M a year, 23 at $5.6M, 16 at $8M. Funded late, it cannot finish inside the horizon at any price
  road_monthly.wear: converges toward an equilibrium at (budget/$1M) x 5% a month, so the budget sets both the destination and the speed: about 13 months to close 90% of the gap at $3.2M a year, 8 at $5M, 4.5 at $8M. Read a mid-flight value as progress, not as failure
  citizen_monthly.satisfaction: a moving average that keeps 70% of last month's value, so about 30% of any change lands in the first month, 66% by the third and 88% by the sixth. A lever changed this turn is roughly two-thirds visible by the next one
  migration_monthly.population: responds to satisfaction, so it carries satisfaction's lag plus its own; population is the last thing to turn around and the last evidence that a policy worked

LOW YIELD -- measured to move the outcome by under 2% across their whole range; set them once and spend the turn budget elsewhere: power_contract_mode, zoning_release

Investigate the city's data, then set the levers you want for this turn.

args.query: SELECT tick, income_tax_rate, property_tax_rate, electricity_tariff, road_maintenance_budget, water_sewer_capex, transit_fare, power_contract_mode FROM lever_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 12
SELECT tick, balance, debt, treasury, road_spend, water_sewer_spend FROM budget_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 12
SELECT tick, wear, congestion FROM road_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC, wear DESC LIMIT 8
SELECT tick, capacity, demand, load_ratio, failure_rate FROM water_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 8
SELECT tick, outage_fraction, demand_kw, supply_kw FROM power_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 6
SELECT tick, satisfaction, employed, disposable_income FROM citizen_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 10

system:
You are the city manager of a simulated city in crisis. Your job is to get the city healthy again within a limited number of turns by adjusting policy levers.

You cannot see the city. Everything you know about it must come from SQL queries against its data warehouse, which records one row per entity per simulated month for the city's entire history. Query it. The history before your first turn shows how the city got into this state, and is usually the fastest route to the cause.

Each turn you may issue several `sql_query` calls, then call `set_levers` with the changes you want. Levers persist between turns, so you only need to set what you are changing. Advancing to the next turn happens automatically once you commit.

Work like an analyst: find what is actually failing before you spend money on it. The city's budget is finite, and a lever set far past what the problem needs will cost more than it repairs. When you have decided, call `set_levers` and briefly say why.

This warehouse is catalogued in DataHub, a metadata platform that records what each table and column means, defines the business terms behind them, and tracks which tables are derived from which. That documentation is reproduced in full below -- it is everything the catalog holds about this warehouse, so there is nothing further to look up.

Use it to skip discovery. You do not need to inspect information_schema or sample tables to work out what a column holds; it is described here. Lineage is generated from the simulation's own causal graph and every edge is verified against the running model, so 'derived from' states a real causal dependency rather than a guess -- it tells you which inputs actually move a given output.

  - started_at: Wall-clock start.
  - finished_at: Wall-clock finish, null while running.

### Glossary
  - Building condition: Visible state band: new, worn, or derelict.
  - Citizen satisfaction: 0–1 well-being of a resident; drives migration.
  - Commute: Home-to-work travel along the road network.
  - Congestion: Traffic load relative to wear-adjusted capacity (0–1).
  - Disposable income: Monthly income remaining after tax and utility/transit bills.
  - Electricity tariff: Retail price charged per kilowatt-hour.
  - Income tax rate: Municipal fraction levied on household gross income.
  - Income tax revenue: Tax collected from household incomes in a month.
  - Migration: Households arriving or leaving in response to city conditions.
  - Municipal budget: City revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury.
  - Power contract mode: Procurement mode: spot, fixed, or hedged.
  - Power outage fraction: Share of electrical demand left unserved.
  - Property tax rate: Annual fraction of building assessed value collected as tax.
  - Road maintenance budget: Annual spend allocated to road repair.
  - Road wear: Pavement degradation on a network segment (0–1).
  - Tile zoning: Land-use designation controlling what may be built.
  - Transit fare: Price charged per transit ride.
  - Water and sewer capex: Annual capital investment in water and sewer capacity.
  - Water load ratio: Water/sewer demand divided by capacity.
  - Zoning release: Share of undeveloped land opened for development.

system:
You are the city manager of a simulated city in crisis. Your job is to get the city healthy again within a limited number of turns by adjusting policy levers.

You cannot see the city. Everything you know about it must come from SQL queries against its data warehouse, which records one row per entity per simulated month for the city's entire history. Query it. The history before your first turn shows how the city got into this state, and is usually the fastest route to the cause.

Each turn you may issue several `sql_query` calls, then call `set_levers` with the changes you want. Levers persist between turns, so you only need to set what you are changing. Advancing to the next turn happens automatically once you commit.

Work like an analyst: find what is actually failing before you spend money on it. The city's budget is finite, and a lever set far past what the problem needs will cost more than it repairs. When you have decided, call `set_levers` and briefly say why.

## Data catalog

This warehouse is catalogued in DataHub, a metadata platform that records what each table and column means, defines the business terms behind them, and tracks which tables are derived from which. That documentation is reproduced in full below -- it is everything the catalog holds about this warehouse, so there is nothing further to look up.

Use it to skip discovery. You do not need to inspect information_schema or sample tables to work out what a column holds; it is described here. Lineage is generated from the simulation's own causal graph and every edge is verified against the running model, so 'derived from' states a real causal dependency rather than a guess -- it tells you which inputs actually move a given output.

### sim_run
One simulation invocation: seed, horizon, grid size, wall-clock bounds.
Columns:
  - run_id: Surrogate key for the run.
  - seed: RNG seed that fully determines the city.
  - years: Simulated years requested.
  - grid_w: Map width in tiles.
  - grid_h: Map height in tiles.
  - started_at: Wall-clock start.
  - finished_at: Wall-clock finish, null while running.
### ticks
Simulated calendar: each row is one month of city time for a run.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Months elapsed from start (0 = initial snapshot).
  - year: 1-based simulated year.
  - month: 1-based month within the year.
### tiles
Spatial grid cells: terrain and zoning. The map the viewer draws.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tile_id: Stable tile id (row-major).
  - x: Grid column.
  - y: Grid row.
  - terrain: grass | water | rock.
  - zoning: none | residential | commercial | industrial | mixed.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.zoning_release -> tiles.zoning
### tile_monthly
Per-tile condition each month: abandonment, utility load, power service.
Columns:

  - abandonment: 0 occupied … 1 abandoned lot.
  - power_served: Whether the tile has power this month.
  - water_load: Local water load proxy.
  - sewer_load: Local sewer load proxy.
### buildings
Structures placed on tiles: type, capacity, assessed value.
Columns:

### Glossary
  - Building condition: Visible state band: new, worn, or derelict.
  - Citizen satisfaction: 0–1 well-being of a resident; drives migration.
  - Commute: Home-to-work travel along the road network.
  - Congestion: Traffic load relative to wear-adjusted capacity (0–1).
  - Disposable income: Monthly income remaining after tax and utility/transit bills.
  - Electricity tariff: Retail price charged per kilowatt-hour.
  - Income tax rate: Municipal fraction levied on household gross income.
  - Income tax revenue: Tax collected from household incomes in a month.
  - Migration: Households arriving or leaving in response to city conditions.
  - Municipal budget: City revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury.
  - Power contract mode: Procurement mode: spot, fixed, or hedged.
  - Power outage fraction: Share of electrical demand left unserved.
  - Property tax rate: Annual fraction of building assessed value collected as tax.
  - Road maintenance budget: Annual spend allocated to road repair.
  - Road wear: Pavement degradation on a network segment (0–1).
  - Tile zoning: Land-use designation controlling what may be built.
  - Transit fare: Price charged per transit ride.
  - Water and sewer capex: Annual capital investment in water and sewer capacity.
  - Water load ratio: Water/sewer demand divided by capacity.
  - Zoning release: Share of undeveloped land opened for development.

system:
You are the city manager of a simulated city in crisis. Your job is to get the city healthy again within a limited number of turns by adjusting policy levers.

You cannot see the city. Everything you know about it must come from SQL queries against its data warehouse, which records one row per entity per simulated month for the city's entire history. Query it. The history before your first turn shows how the city got into this state, and is usually the fastest route to the cause.

Each turn you may issue several `sql_query` calls, then call `set_levers` with the changes you want. Levers persist between turns, so you only need to set what you are changing. Advancing to the next turn happens automatically once you commit.

Work like an analyst: find what is actually failing before you spend money on it. The city's budget is finite, and a lever set far past what the problem needs will cost more than it repairs. When you have decided, call `set_levers` and briefly say why.

## Data catalog

This warehouse is catalogued in DataHub, a metadata platform that records what each table and column means, defines the business terms behind them, and tracks which tables are derived from which. That documentation is reproduced in full below -- it is everything the catalog holds about this warehouse, so there is nothing further to look up.

Use it to skip discovery. You do not need to inspect information_schema or sample tables to work out what a column holds; it is described here. Lineage is generated from the simulation's own causal graph and every edge is verified against the running model, so 'derived from' states a real causal dependency rather than a guess -- it tells you which inputs actually move a given output.

### sim_run
One simulation invocation: seed, horizon, grid size, wall-clock bounds.
Columns:
  - run_id: Surrogate key for the run.
  - seed: RNG seed that fully determines the city.
  - years: Simulated years requested.
  - grid_w: Map width in tiles.
  - grid_h: Map height in tiles.
  - started_at: Wall-clock start.
  - finished_at: Wall-clock finish, null while running.
### ticks
Simulated calendar: each row is one month of city time for a run.
Columns:

  - year: 1-based simulated year.
  - month: 1-based month within the year.
### tiles
Spatial grid cells: terrain and zoning. The map the viewer draws.
Columns:

  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - capacity: System capacity units.
  - demand: System demand units.
  - load_ratio: demand / capacity.
  - failure_rate: Stress-driven failure proxy.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.water_sewer_capex -> water_monthly.capacity
  water_monthly.capacity -> water_monthly.load_ratio
### migration_monthly
Household arrivals and departures, net migration, population.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - arrivals: People arriving.
  - departures: People leaving.
  - net: arrivals − departures.
  - population: Population after migration.
Derived from: citizen_monthly
  citizen_monthly.satisfaction -> migration_monthly.net

### Glossary
  - Building condition: Visible state band: new, worn, or derelict.
  - Citizen satisfaction: 0–1 well-being of a resident; drives migration.
  - Commute: Home-to-work travel along the road network.
  - Congestion: Traffic load relative to wear-adjusted capacity (0–1).
  - Disposable income: Monthly income remaining after tax and utility/transit bills.
  - Electricity tariff: Retail price charged per kilowatt-hour.
  - Income tax rate: Municipal fraction levied on household gross income.
  - Income tax revenue: Tax collected from household incomes in a month.
  - Migration: Households arriving or leaving in response to city conditions.
  - Municipal budget: City revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury.
  - Power contract mode: Procurement mode: spot, fixed, or hedged.
  - Power outage fraction: Share of electrical demand left unserved.
  - Property tax rate: Annual fraction of building assessed value collected as tax.
  - Road maintenance budget: Annual spend allocated to road repair.
  - Road wear: Pavement degradation on a network segment (0–1).
  - Tile zoning: Land-use designation controlling what may be built.
  - Transit fare: Price charged per transit ride.
  - Water and sewer capex: Annual capital investment in water and sewer capacity.
  - Water load ratio: Water/sewer demand divided by capacity.
  - Zoning release: Share of undeveloped land opened for development.

system:
You are the city manager of a simulated city in crisis. Your job is to get the city healthy again within a limited number of turns by adjusting policy levers.

You cannot see the city. Everything you know about it must come from SQL queries against its data warehouse, which records one row per entity per simulated month for the city's entire history. Query it. The history before your first turn shows how the city got into this state, and is usually the fastest route to the cause.

Each turn you may issue several `sql_query` calls, then call `set_levers` with the changes you want. Levers persist between turns, so you only need to set what you are changing. Advancing to the next turn happens automatically once you commit.

Work like an analyst: find what is actually failing before you spend money on it. The city's budget is finite, and a lever set far past what the problem needs will cost more than it repairs. When you have decided, call `set_levers` and briefly say why.

## Data catalog

This warehouse is catalogued in DataHub, a metadata platform that records what each table and column means, defines the business terms behind them, and tracks which tables are derived from which. That documentation is reproduced in full below -- it is everything the catalog holds about this warehouse, so there is nothing further to look up.

Use it to skip discovery. You do not need to inspect information_schema or sample tables to work out what a column holds; it is described here. Lineage is generated from the simulation's own causal graph and every edge is verified against the running model, so 'derived from' states a real causal dependency rather than a guess -- it tells you which inputs actually move a given output.

### sim_run
One simulation invocation: seed, horizon, grid size, wall-clock bounds.
Columns:
  - run_id: Surrogate key for the run.
  - seed: RNG seed that fully determines the city.
  - years: Simulated years requested.
  - grid_w: Map width in tiles.
  - grid_h: Map height in tiles.
  - started_at: Wall-clock start.
  - finished_at: Wall-clock finish, null while running.
### ticks
Simulated calendar: each row is one month of city time for a run.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Months elapsed from start (0 = initial snapshot).
  - year: 1-based simulated year.
  - month: 1-based month within the year.
### tiles
Spatial grid cells: terrain and zoning. The map the viewer draws.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tile_id: Stable tile id (row-major).
  - x: Grid column.
  - y: Grid row.
  - terrain: grass | water | rock.
  - zoning: none | residential | commercial | industrial | mixed.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.zoning_release -> tiles.zoning
### tile_monthly
Per-tile condition each month: abandonment, utility load, power service.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - tile_id: Tile.
  - condition: 0 new … 1 ruined appearance.
  - abandonment: 0 occupied … 1 abandoned lot.
  - power_served: Whether the tile has power this month.
  - water_load: Local water load proxy.
  - sewer_load: Local sewer load proxy.
### buildings
Structures placed on tiles: type, capacity, assessed value.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - building_id: Stable building id.
  - tile_id: Tile the building occupies.
  - building_type: residential | commercial | industrial | civic.
  - capacity: Occupancy or job capacity.
  - assessed_value: Tax assessment base.
Derived from: tiles
  tiles.zoning -> buildings.building_id
### building_monthly
Building condition and service each month — what the viewer shades.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - building_id: Building.
  - condition_band: new | worn | derelict.
  - condition_score: 0 new … 1 derelict.
  - occupancy: Current occupants or workers.
  - power_served: Electrified this month.
  - power_demand_kw: Electrical demand.
  - water_demand: Water demand units.
Derived from: power_monthly
  power_monthly.outage_fraction -> building_monthly.power_served
### households
Households located at a home tile and building.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - household_id: Stable household id.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile.
  - home_building_id: Home building.
### citizens
Individual people belonging to households.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - citizen_id: Stable citizen id.
  - household_id: Household membership.
### citizen_monthly
Jobs, income, satisfaction, and map position each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - citizen_id: Citizen.
  - household_id: Household.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile this month.
  - workplace_tile_id: Workplace tile.
  - job_sector: Employment sector.
  - income: Annual gross income.
  - disposable_income: Monthly income after tax and bills.
  - satisfaction: 0–1 well-being score.
  - pos_x: Map x position.
  - pos_y: Map y position.
  - employed: Employment flag.
  - uses_transit: Commute mode includes transit.
Derived from: building_monthly, commute_monthly, lever_monthly, migration_monthly, water_monthly
  building_monthly.power_served -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  citizen_monthly.disposable_income -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  commute_monthly.travel_time -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.electricity_tariff -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.income_tax_rate -> citizen_monthly.disposable_income
  lever_monthly.property_tax_rate -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.transit_fare -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  migration_monthly.net -> citizen_monthly.citizen_id
  water_monthly.load_ratio -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
### road_segments
Road network edges on the grid.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - segment_id: Stable segment id.
  - from_tile_id: Start tile.
  - to_tile_id: End tile.
  - from_x: Start x.
  - from_y: Start y.
  - to_x: End x.
  - to_y: End y.
### road_monthly
Traffic, wear, and congestion per segment per month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - segment_id: Road segment.
  - traffic: Traffic volume.
  - wear: 0 smooth … 1 ruined pavement.
  - congestion: 0 free-flow … 1 jammed.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.road_maintenance_budget -> road_monthly.wear
  road_monthly.wear -> road_monthly.congestion
### commute_monthly
Home↔work commute outcomes for each citizen each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - citizen_id: Citizen.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile.
  - workplace_tile_id: Workplace tile.
  - travel_time: Commute duration units.
  - uses_transit: Transit rider flag.
Derived from: road_monthly
  road_monthly.congestion -> commute_monthly.travel_time
### budget_monthly
Municipal revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - income_tax_revenue: Income tax collected.
  - property_tax_revenue: Property tax collected.
  - utility_revenue: Electricity bill revenue.
  - transit_revenue: Transit fare revenue.
  - road_spend: Road maintenance spend.
  - water_sewer_spend: Water/sewer capital spend.
  - other_spend: Other municipal spend.
  - balance: Revenue minus spend.
  - debt: Outstanding debt.
  - treasury: Cash on hand.
Derived from: citizen_monthly, lever_monthly
  budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue -> budget_monthly.balance
  budget_monthly.property_tax_revenue -> budget_monthly.balance
  citizen_monthly.citizen_id -> budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue
  citizen_monthly.income -> budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue
  lever_monthly.electricity_tariff -> budget_monthly.utility_revenue

  lever_monthly.property_tax_rate -> budget_monthly.property_tax_revenue

  lever_monthly.water_sewer_capex -> budget_monthly.water_sewer_spend
### lever_monthly
Player lever positions in force each month (policy inputs).
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - income_tax_rate: Fraction tax on income.
  - property_tax_rate: Annual fraction of assessed value.
  - electricity_tariff: Retail currency per kWh.
  - road_maintenance_budget: Annual road spend.
  - water_sewer_capex: Annual water/sewer capital.
  - transit_fare: Fare per ride.
  - zoning_release: Share of land opened.
  - power_contract_mode: 0 spot, 1 fixed, 2 hedged.
### power_monthly
City-wide electricity demand, supply, outages, contract, tariff.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - demand_kw: Aggregate demand.
  - supply_kw: Available supply.
  - outage_fraction: Share of demand unserved.
  - contract_mode: spot | fixed | hedged.
  - tariff: Retail tariff in force.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.power_contract_mode -> power_monthly.outage_fraction
### water_monthly
Water and sewer capacity, demand, load ratio, failure rate.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - capacity: System capacity units.
  - demand: System demand units.
  - load_ratio: demand / capacity.
  - failure_rate: Stress-driven failure proxy.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.water_sewer_capex -> water_monthly.capacity
  water_monthly.capacity -> water_monthly.load_ratio
### migration_monthly
Household arrivals and departures, net migration, population.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - arrivals: People arriving.
  - departures: People leaving.
  - net: arrivals − departures.
  - population: Population after migration.
Derived from: citizen_monthly
  citizen_monthly.satisfaction -> migration_monthly.net

### Glossary
  - Building condition: Visible state band: new, worn, or derelict.
  - Citizen satisfaction: 0–1 well-being of a resident; drives migration.
  - Commute: Home-to-work travel along the road network.
  - Congestion: Traffic load relative to wear-adjusted capacity (0–1).
  - Disposable income: Monthly income remaining after tax and utility/transit bills.
  - Electricity tariff: Retail price charged per kilowatt-hour.
  - Income tax rate: Municipal fraction levied on household gross income.
  - Income tax revenue: Tax collected from household incomes in a month.
  - Migration: Households arriving or leaving in response to city conditions.
  - Municipal budget: City revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury.
  - Power contract mode: Procurement mode: spot, fixed, or hedged.
  - Power outage fraction: Share of electrical demand left unserved.
  - Property tax rate: Annual fraction of building assessed value collected as tax.
  - Road maintenance budget: Annual spend allocated to road repair.
  - Road wear: Pavement degradation on a network segment (0–1).
  - Tile zoning: Land-use designation controlling what may be built.
  - Transit fare: Price charged per transit ride.
  - Water and sewer capex: Annual capital investment in water and sewer capacity.
  - Water load ratio: Water/sewer demand divided by capacity.
  - Zoning release: Share of undeveloped land opened for development.

system:
You are the city manager of a simulated city in crisis. Your job is to get the city healthy again within a limited number of turns by adjusting policy levers.

You cannot see the city. Everything you know about it must come from SQL queries against its data warehouse, which records one row per entity per simulated month for the city's entire history. Query it. The history before your first turn shows how the city got into this state, and is usually the fastest route to the cause.

Each turn you may issue several `sql_query` calls, then call `set_levers` with the changes you want. Levers persist between turns, so you only need to set what you are changing. Advancing to the next turn happens automatically once you commit.

Work like an analyst: find what is actually failing before you spend money on it. The city's budget is finite, and a lever set far past what the problem needs will cost more than it repairs. When you have decided, call `set_levers` and briefly say why.

## Data catalog

This warehouse is catalogued in DataHub, a metadata platform that records what each table and column means, defines the business terms behind them, and tracks which tables are derived from which. That documentation is reproduced in full below -- it is everything the catalog holds about this warehouse, so there is nothing further to look up.

Use it to skip discovery. You do not need to inspect information_schema or sample tables to work out what a column holds; it is described here. Lineage is generated from the simulation's own causal graph and every edge is verified against the running model, so 'derived from' states a real causal dependency rather than a guess -- it tells you which inputs actually move a given output.

### sim_run
One simulation invocation: seed, horizon, grid size, wall-clock bounds.
Columns:
  - run_id: Surrogate key for the run.
  - seed: RNG seed that fully determines the city.
  - years: Simulated years requested.
  - grid_w: Map width in tiles.
  - grid_h: Map height in tiles.
  - started_at: Wall-clock start.
  - finished_at: Wall-clock finish, null while running.
### ticks
Simulated calendar: each row is one month of city time for a run.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Months elapsed from start (0 = initial snapshot).
  - year: 1-based simulated year.
  - month: 1-based month within the year.
### tiles
Spatial grid cells: terrain and zoning. The map the viewer draws.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tile_id: Stable tile id (row-major).
  - x: Grid column.
  - y: Grid row.
  - terrain: grass | water | rock.
  - zoning: none | residential | commercial | industrial | mixed.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.zoning_release -> tiles.zoning
### tile_monthly
Per-tile condition each month: abandonment, utility load, power service.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - tile_id: Tile.
  - condition: 0 new … 1 ruined appearance.
  - abandonment: 0 occupied … 1 abandoned lot.
  - power_served: Whether the tile has power this month.
  - water_load: Local water load proxy.
  - sewer_load: Local sewer load proxy.
### buildings
Structures placed on tiles: type, capacity, assessed value.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - building_id: Stable building id.
  - tile_id: Tile the building occupies.
  - building_type: residential | commercial | industrial | civic.
  - capacity: Occupancy or job capacity.
  - assessed_value: Tax assessment base.
Derived from: tiles
  tiles.zoning -> buildings.building_id
### building_monthly
Building condition and service each month — what the viewer shades.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - building_id: Building.
  - condition_band: new | worn | derelict.
  - condition_score: 0 new … 1 derelict.
  - occupancy: Current occupants or workers.
  - power_served: Electrified this month.
  - power_demand_kw: Electrical demand.
  - water_demand: Water demand units.
Derived from: power_monthly
  power_monthly.outage_fraction -> building_monthly.power_served
### households
Households located at a home tile and building.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - household_id: Stable household id.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile.
  - home_building_id: Home building.
### citizens
Individual people belonging to households.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - citizen_id: Stable citizen id.
  - household_id: Household membership.
### citizen_monthly
Jobs, income, satisfaction, and map position each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - citizen_id: Citizen.
  - household_id: Household.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile this month.
  - workplace_tile_id: Workplace tile.
  - job_sector: Employment sector.
  - income: Annual gross income.
  - disposable_income: Monthly income after tax and bills.
  - satisfaction: 0–1 well-being score.
  - pos_x: Map x position.
  - pos_y: Map y position.
  - employed: Employment flag.
  - uses_transit: Commute mode includes transit.
Derived from: building_monthly, commute_monthly, lever_monthly, migration_monthly, water_monthly
  building_monthly.power_served -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  citizen_monthly.disposable_income -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  commute_monthly.travel_time -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.electricity_tariff -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.income_tax_rate -> citizen_monthly.disposable_income
  lever_monthly.property_tax_rate -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.transit_fare -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  migration_monthly.net -> citizen_monthly.citizen_id
  water_monthly.load_ratio -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
### road_segments
Road network edges on the grid.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - segment_id: Stable segment id.
  - from_tile_id: Start tile.
  - to_tile_id: End tile.
  - from_x: Start x.
  - from_y: Start y.
  - to_x: End x.
  - to_y: End y.
### road_monthly
Traffic, wear, and congestion per segment per month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - segment_id: Road segment.
  - traffic: Traffic volume.
  - wear: 0 smooth … 1 ruined pavement.
  - congestion: 0 free-flow … 1 jammed.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.road_maintenance_budget -> road_monthly.wear
  road_monthly.wear -> road_monthly.congestion
### commute_monthly
Home↔work commute outcomes for each citizen each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - citizen_id: Citizen.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile.
  - workplace_tile_id: Workplace tile.
  - travel_time: Commute duration units.
  - uses_transit: Transit rider flag.
Derived from: road_monthly
  road_monthly.congestion -> commute_monthly.travel_time
### budget_monthly
Municipal revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - income_tax_revenue: Income tax collected.
  - property_tax_revenue: Property tax collected.
  - utility_revenue: Electricity bill revenue.
  - transit_revenue: Transit fare revenue.
  - road_spend: Road maintenance spend.
  - water_sewer_spend: Water/sewer capital spend.
  - other_spend: Other municipal spend.
  - balance: Revenue minus spend.
  - debt: Outstanding debt.
  - treasury: Cash on hand.
Derived from: citizen_monthly, lever_monthly
  budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue -> budget_monthly.balance
  budget_monthly.property_tax_revenue -> budget_monthly.balance
  citizen_monthly.citizen_id -> budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue
  citizen_monthly.income -> budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue
  lever_monthly.electricity_tariff -> budget_monthly.utility_revenue
  lever_monthly.income_tax_rate -> budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue
  lever_monthly.property_tax_rate -> budget_monthly.property_tax_revenue
  lever_monthly.road_maintenance_budget -> budget_monthly.road_spend
  lever_monthly.transit_fare -> budget_monthly.transit_revenue
  lever_monthly.water_sewer_capex -> budget_monthly.water_sewer_spend
### lever_monthly
Player lever positions in force each month (policy inputs).
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - income_tax_rate: Fraction tax on income.
  - property_tax_rate: Annual fraction of assessed value.
  - electricity_tariff: Retail currency per kWh.
  - road_maintenance_budget: Annual road spend.
  - water_sewer_capex: Annual water/sewer capital.
  - transit_fare: Fare per ride.
  - zoning_release: Share of land opened.
  - power_contract_mode: 0 spot, 1 fixed, 2 hedged.
### power_monthly
City-wide electricity demand, supply, outages, contract, tariff.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - demand_kw: Aggregate demand.
  - supply_kw: Available supply.
  - outage_fraction: Share of demand unserved.
  - contract_mode: spot | fixed | hedged.
  - tariff: Retail tariff in force.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.power_contract_mode -> power_monthly.outage_fraction
### water_monthly
Water and sewer capacity, demand, load ratio, failure rate.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - capacity: System capacity units.
  - demand: System demand units.
  - load_ratio: demand / capacity.
  - failure_rate: Stress-driven failure proxy.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.water_sewer_capex -> water_monthly.capacity
  water_monthly.capacity -> water_monthly.load_ratio
### migration_monthly
Household arrivals and departures, net migration, population.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - arrivals: People arriving.
  - departures: People leaving.
  - net: arrivals − departures.
  - population: Population after migration.
Derived from: citizen_monthly
  citizen_monthly.satisfaction -> migration_monthly.net

### Glossary
  - Building condition: Visible state band: new, worn, or derelict.
  - Citizen satisfaction: 0–1 well-being of a resident; drives migration.
  - Commute: Home-to-work travel along the road network.
  - Congestion: Traffic load relative to wear-adjusted capacity (0–1).
  - Disposable income: Monthly income remaining after tax and utility/transit bills.
  - Electricity tariff: Retail price charged per kilowatt-hour.
  - Income tax rate: Municipal fraction levied on household gross income.
  - Income tax revenue: Tax collected from household incomes in a month.
  - Migration: Households arriving or leaving in response to city conditions.
  - Municipal budget: City revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury.
  - Power contract mode: Procurement mode: spot, fixed, or hedged.
  - Power outage fraction: Share of electrical demand left unserved.
  - Property tax rate: Annual fraction of building assessed value collected as tax.
  - Road maintenance budget: Annual spend allocated to road repair.
  - Road wear: Pavement degradation on a network segment (0–1).
  - Tile zoning: Land-use designation controlling what may be built.
  - Transit fare: Price charged per transit ride.
  - Water and sewer capex: Annual capital investment in water and sewer capacity.
  - Water load ratio: Water/sewer demand divided by capacity.
  - Zoning release: Share of undeveloped land opened for development.

system:
You are the city manager of a simulated city in crisis. Your job is to get the city healthy again within a limited number of turns by adjusting policy levers.

You cannot see the city. Everything you know about it must come from SQL queries against its data warehouse, which records one row per entity per simulated month for the city's entire history. Query it. The history before your first turn shows how the city got into this state, and is usually the fastest route to the cause.

Each turn you may issue several `sql_query` calls, then call `set_levers` with the changes you want. Levers persist between turns, so you only need to set what you are changing. Advancing to the next turn happens automatically once you commit.

Work like an analyst: find what is actually failing before you spend money on it. The city's budget is finite, and a lever set far past what the problem needs will cost more than it repairs. When you have decided, call `set_levers` and briefly say why.

## Data catalog

This warehouse is catalogued in DataHub, a metadata platform that records what each table and column means, defines the business terms behind them, and tracks which tables are derived from which. That documentation is reproduced in full below -- it is everything the catalog holds about this warehouse, so there is nothing further to look up.

Use it to skip discovery. You do not need to inspect information_schema or sample tables to work out what a column holds; it is described here. Lineage is generated from the simulation's own causal graph and every edge is verified against the running model, so 'derived from' states a real causal dependency rather than a guess -- it tells you which inputs actually move a given output.

### sim_run
One simulation invocation: seed, horizon, grid size, wall-clock bounds.
Columns:
  - run_id: Surrogate key for the run.
  - seed: RNG seed that fully determines the city.
  - years: Simulated years requested.
  - grid_w: Map width in tiles.
  - grid_h: Map height in tiles.
  - started_at: Wall-clock start.
  - finished_at: Wall-clock finish, null while running.
### ticks
Simulated calendar: each row is one month of city time for a run.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Months elapsed from start (0 = initial snapshot).
  - year: 1-based simulated year.
  - month: 1-based month within the year.
### tiles
Spatial grid cells: terrain and zoning. The map the viewer draws.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tile_id: Stable tile id (row-major).
  - x: Grid column.
  - y: Grid row.
  - terrain: grass | water | rock.
  - zoning: none | residential | commercial | industrial | mixed.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.zoning_release -> tiles.zoning
### tile_monthly
Per-tile condition each month: abandonment, utility load, power service.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.

  - assessed_value: Tax assessment base.

Building condition and service each month — what the viewer shades.

Individual people belonging to households.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - citizen_id: Stable citizen id.
  - household_id: Household membership.

  - road_maintenance_budget: Annual road spend.
  - water_sewer_capex: Annual water/sewer capital.
  - transit_fare: Fare per ride.
  - zoning_release: Share of land opened.
  - power_contract_mode: 0 spot, 1 fixed, 2 hedged.

City-wide electricity demand, supply, outages, contract, tariff.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - demand_kw: Aggregate demand.
  - supply_kw: Available supply.
  - outage_fraction: Share of demand unserved.
  - contract_mode: spot | fixed | hedged.
  - tariff: Retail tariff in force.
Derived from: lever_monthly

### water_monthly
Water and sewer capacity, demand, load ratio, failure rate.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - capacity: System capacity units.
  - demand: System demand units.
  - load_ratio: demand / capacity.
  - failure_rate: Stress-driven failure proxy.
Derived from: lever_monthly

  water_monthly.capacity -> water_monthly.load_ratio
### migration_monthly
Household arrivals and departures, net migration, population.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - arrivals: People arriving.
  - departures: People leaving.
  - net: arrivals − departures.
  - population: Population after migration.
Derived from: citizen_monthly
  citizen_monthly.satisfaction -> migration_monthly.net

### Glossary
  - Building condition: Visible state band: new, worn, or derelict.
  - Citizen satisfaction: 0–1 well-being of a resident; drives migration.
  - Commute: Home-to-work travel along the road network.
  - Congestion: Traffic load relative to wear-adjusted capacity (0–1).
  - Disposable income: Monthly income remaining after tax and utility/transit bills.
  - Electricity tariff: Retail price charged per kilowatt-hour.
  - Income tax rate: Municipal fraction levied on household gross income.
  - Income tax revenue: Tax collected from household incomes in a month.
  - Migration: Households arriving or leaving in response to city conditions.
  - Municipal budget: City revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury.
  - Power contract mode: Procurement mode: spot, fixed, or hedged.
  - Power outage fraction: Share of electrical demand left unserved.
  - Property tax rate: Annual fraction of building assessed value collected as tax.
  - Road maintenance budget: Annual spend allocated to road repair.
  - Road wear: Pavement degradation on a network segment (0–1).
  - Tile zoning: Land-use designation controlling what may be built.
  - Transit fare: Price charged per transit ride.
  - Water and sewer capex: Annual capital investment in water and sewer capacity.
  - Water load ratio: Water/sewer demand divided by capacity.
  - Zoning release: Share of undeveloped land opened for development.

  electricity_tariff = 0.65 -- above the documented range 0-0.1 [moderate]. the worst revenue lever in the city and the easiest to mistake for a good one. Treat it as a price to keep low, never as a way to fund the recovery
  transit_fare = 8 -- above the documented range 0-2 [moderate]. a pure transfer: it collects exactly what it removes from riders' disposable income, about $22,000 a month per unit of fare in each direction, and the satisfaction penalty on the third of citizens who ride is unrecovered. system:
You are the city manager of a simulated city in crisis. Your job is to get the city healthy again within a limited number of turns by adjusting policy levers.

You cannot see the city. Everything you know about it must come from SQL queries against its data warehouse, which records one row per entity per simulated month for the city's entire history. Query it. The history before your first turn shows how the city got into this state, and is usually the fastest route to the cause.

Each turn you may issue several `sql_query` calls, then call `set_levers` with the changes you want. Levers persist between turns, so you only need to set what you are changing. Advancing to the next turn happens automatically once you commit.

Work like an analyst: find what is actually failing before you spend money on it. The city's budget is finite, and a lever set far past what the problem needs will cost more than it repairs. When you have decided, call `set_levers` and briefly say why.

## Data catalog

This warehouse is catalogued in DataHub, a metadata platform that records what each table and column means, defines the business terms behind them, and tracks which tables are derived from which. That documentation is reproduced in full below -- it is everything the catalog holds about this warehouse, so there is nothing further to look up.

Use it to skip discovery. You do not need to inspect information_schema or sample tables to work out what a column holds; it is described here. Lineage is generated from the simulation's own causal graph and every edge is verified against the running model, so 'derived from' states a real causal dependency rather than a guess -- it tells you which inputs actually move a given output.

### sim_run
One simulation invocation: seed, horizon, grid size, wall-clock bounds.
Columns:
  - run_id: Surrogate key for the run.
  - seed: RNG seed that fully determines the city.
  - years: Simulated years requested.
  - grid_w: Map width in tiles.
  - grid_h: Map height in tiles.
  - started_at: Wall-clock start.
  - finished_at: Wall-clock finish, null while running.
### ticks
Simulated calendar: each row is one month of city time for a run.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Months elapsed from start (0 = initial snapshot).
  - year: 1-based simulated year.
  - month: 1-based month within the year.
### tiles
Spatial grid cells: terrain and zoning. The map the viewer draws.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tile_id: Stable tile id (row-major).
  - x: Grid column.
  - y: Grid row.
  - terrain: grass | water | rock.
  - zoning: none | residential | commercial | industrial | mixed.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.zoning_release -> tiles.zoning
### tile_monthly
Per-tile condition each month: abandonment, utility load, power service.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - tile_id: Tile.
  - condition: 0 new … 1 ruined appearance.
  - abandonment: 0 occupied … 1 abandoned lot.
  - power_served: Whether the tile has power this month.
  - water_load: Local water load proxy.
  - sewer_load: Local sewer load proxy.
### buildings
Structures placed on tiles: type, capacity, assessed value.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - building_id: Stable building id.
  - tile_id: Tile the building occupies.
  - building_type: residential | commercial | industrial | civic.
  - capacity: Occupancy or job capacity.
  - assessed_value: Tax assessment base.
Derived from: tiles
  tiles.zoning -> buildings.building_id
### building_monthly
Building condition and service each month — what the viewer shades.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - building_id: Building.

  - home_building_id: Home building.
### citizens
Individual people belonging to households.
Columns:

  - citizen_id: Stable citizen id.

Water and sewer capacity, demand, load ratio, failure rate.
Columns:

  - capacity: System capacity units.
  - demand: System demand units.
  - load_ratio: demand / capacity.
  - failure_rate: Stress-driven failure proxy.
Derived from: lever_monthly

### migration_monthly
Household arrivals and departures, net migration, population.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - arrivals: People arriving.
  - departures: People leaving.
  - net: arrivals − departures.
  - population: Population after migration.
Derived from: citizen_monthly
  citizen_monthly.satisfaction -> migration_monthly.net

### Glossary
  - Building condition: Visible state band: new, worn, or derelict.
  - Citizen satisfaction: 0–1 well-being of a resident; drives migration.
  - Commute: Home-to-work travel along the road network.
  - Congestion: Traffic load relative to wear-adjusted capacity (0–1).
  - Disposable income: Monthly income remaining after tax and utility/transit bills.
  - Electricity tariff: Retail price charged per kilowatt-hour.
  - Income tax rate: Municipal fraction levied on household gross income.
  - Income tax revenue: Tax collected from household incomes in a month.
  - Migration: Households arriving or leaving in response to city conditions.
  - Municipal budget: City revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury.
  - Power contract mode: Procurement mode: spot, fixed, or hedged.
  - Power outage fraction: Share of electrical demand left unserved.
  - Property tax rate: Annual fraction of building assessed value collected as tax.
  - Road maintenance budget: Annual spend allocated to road repair.
  - Road wear: Pavement degradation on a network segment (0–1).
  - Tile zoning: Land-use designation controlling what may be built.
  - Transit fare: Price charged per transit ride.
  - Water and sewer capex: Annual capital investment in water and sewer capacity.
  - Water load ratio: Water/sewer demand divided by capacity.
  - Zoning release: Share of undeveloped land opened for development.

system:
You are the city manager of a simulated city in crisis. Your job is to get the city healthy again within a limited number of turns by adjusting policy levers.

You cannot see the city. Everything you know about it must come from SQL queries against its data warehouse, which records one row per entity per simulated month for the city's entire history. Query it. The history before your first turn shows how the city got into this state, and is usually the fastest route to the cause.

Each turn you may issue several `sql_query` calls, then call `set_levers` with the changes you want. Levers persist between turns, so you only need to set what you are changing. Advancing to the next turn happens automatically once you commit.

Work like an analyst: find what is actually failing before you spend money on it. The city's budget is finite, and a lever set far past what the problem needs will cost more than it repairs. When you have decided, call `set_levers` and briefly say why.

## Data catalog

This warehouse is catalogued in DataHub, a metadata platform that records what each table and column means, defines the business terms behind them, and tracks which tables are derived from which. That documentation is reproduced in full below -- it is everything the catalog holds about this warehouse, so there is nothing further to look up.

Use it to skip discovery. You do not need to inspect information_schema or sample tables to work out what a column holds; it is described here. Lineage is generated from the simulation's own causal graph and every edge is verified against the running model, so 'derived from' states a real causal dependency rather than a guess -- it tells you which inputs actually move a given output.

### sim_run
One simulation invocation: seed, horizon, grid size, wall-clock bounds.
Columns:
  - run_id: Surrogate key for the run.
  - seed: RNG seed that fully determines the city.
  - years: Simulated years requested.
  - grid_w: Map width in tiles.
  - grid_h: Map height in tiles.
  - started_at: Wall-clock start.
  - finished_at: Wall-clock finish, null while running.
### ticks
Simulated calendar: each row is one month of city time for a run.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Months elapsed from start (0 = initial snapshot).
  - year: 1-based simulated year.
  - month: 1-based month within the year.
### tiles
Spatial grid cells: terrain and zoning. The map the viewer draws.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tile_id: Stable tile id (row-major).
  - x: Grid column.
  - y: Grid row.
  - terrain: grass | water | rock.
  - zoning: none | residential | commercial | industrial | mixed.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.zoning_release -> tiles.zoning
### tile_monthly
Per-tile condition each month: abandonment, utility load, power service.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - tile_id: Tile.
  - condition: 0 new … 1 ruined appearance.
  - abandonment: 0 occupied … 1 abandoned lot.
  - power_served: Whether the tile has power this month.
  - water_load: Local water load proxy.
  - sewer_load: Local sewer load proxy.
### buildings
Structures placed on tiles: type, capacity, assessed value.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - building_id: Stable building id.
  - tile_id: Tile the building occupies.
  - building_type: residential | commercial | industrial | civic.
  - capacity: Occupancy or job capacity.
  - assessed_value: Tax assessment base.
Derived from: tiles
  tiles.zoning -> buildings.building_id
### building_monthly
Building condition and service each month — what the viewer shades.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - building_id: Building.
  - condition_band: new | worn | derelict.
  - condition_score: 0 new … 1 derelict.
  - occupancy: Current occupants or workers.
  - power_served: Electrified this month.
  - power_demand_kw: Electrical demand.
  - water_demand: Water demand units.
Derived from: power_monthly
  power_monthly.outage_fraction -> building_monthly.power_served
### households
Households located at a home tile and building.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - household_id: Stable household id.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile.
  - home_building_id: Home building.
### citizens
Individual people belonging to households.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - citizen_id: Stable citizen id.
  - household_id: Household membership.
### citizen_monthly
Jobs, income, satisfaction, and map position each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - citizen_id: Citizen.
  - household_id: Household.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile this month.
  - workplace_tile_id: Workplace tile.
  - job_sector: Employment sector.
  - income: Annual gross income.
  - disposable_income: Monthly income after tax and bills.
  - satisfaction: 0–1 well-being score.
  - pos_x: Map x position.
  - pos_y: Map y position.
  - employed: Employment flag.
  - uses_transit: Commute mode includes transit.
Derived from: building_monthly, commute_monthly, lever_monthly, migration_monthly, water_monthly
  building_monthly.power_served -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  citizen_monthly.disposable_income -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  commute_monthly.travel_time -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.electricity_tariff -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.income_tax_rate -> citizen_monthly.disposable_income
  lever_monthly.property_tax_rate -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  lever_monthly.transit_fare -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
  migration_monthly.net -> citizen_monthly.citizen_id
  water_monthly.load_ratio -> citizen_monthly.satisfaction
### road_segments
Road network edges on the grid.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - segment_id: Stable segment id.
  - from_tile_id: Start tile.
  - to_tile_id: End tile.
  - from_x: Start x.
  - from_y: Start y.
  - to_x: End x.
  - to_y: End y.
### road_monthly
Traffic, wear, and congestion per segment per month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - segment_id: Road segment.
  - traffic: Traffic volume.
  - wear: 0 smooth … 1 ruined pavement.
  - congestion: 0 free-flow … 1 jammed.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.road_maintenance_budget -> road_monthly.wear
  road_monthly.wear -> road_monthly.congestion
### commute_monthly
Home↔work commute outcomes for each citizen each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - citizen_id: Citizen.
  - home_tile_id: Home tile.
  - workplace_tile_id: Workplace tile.
  - travel_time: Commute duration units.
  - uses_transit: Transit rider flag.
Derived from: road_monthly
  road_monthly.congestion -> commute_monthly.travel_time
### budget_monthly
Municipal revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury each month.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - income_tax_revenue: Income tax collected.
  - property_tax_revenue: Property tax collected.
  - utility_revenue: Electricity bill revenue.
  - transit_revenue: Transit fare revenue.
  - road_spend: Road maintenance spend.
  - water_sewer_spend: Water/sewer capital spend.
  - other_spend: Other municipal spend.
  - balance: Revenue minus spend.
  - debt: Outstanding debt.
  - treasury: Cash on hand.
Derived from: citizen_monthly, lever_monthly
  budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue -> budget_monthly.balance
  budget_monthly.property_tax_revenue -> budget_monthly.balance
  citizen_monthly.citizen_id -> budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue
  citizen_monthly.income -> budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue
  lever_monthly.electricity_tariff -> budget_monthly.utility_revenue
  lever_monthly.income_tax_rate -> budget_monthly.income_tax_revenue
  lever_monthly.property_tax_rate -> budget_monthly.property_tax_revenue
  lever_monthly.road_maintenance_budget -> budget_monthly.road_spend
  lever_monthly.transit_fare -> budget_monthly.transit_revenue
  lever_monthly.water_sewer_capex -> budget_monthly.water_sewer_spend
### lever_monthly
Player lever positions in force each month (policy inputs).
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - income_tax_rate: Fraction tax on income.
  - property_tax_rate: Annual fraction of assessed value.
  - electricity_tariff: Retail currency per kWh.
  - road_maintenance_budget: Annual road spend.
  - water_sewer_capex: Annual water/sewer capital.
  - transit_fare: Fare per ride.
  - zoning_release: Share of land opened.
  - power_contract_mode: 0 spot, 1 fixed, 2 hedged.
### power_monthly
City-wide electricity demand, supply, outages, contract, tariff.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - demand_kw: Aggregate demand.
  - supply_kw: Available supply.
  - outage_fraction: Share of demand unserved.
  - contract_mode: spot | fixed | hedged.
  - tariff: Retail tariff in force.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.power_contract_mode -> power_monthly.outage_fraction
### water_monthly
Water and sewer capacity, demand, load ratio, failure rate.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - capacity: System capacity units.
  - demand: System demand units.
  - load_ratio: demand / capacity.
  - failure_rate: Stress-driven failure proxy.
Derived from: lever_monthly
  lever_monthly.water_sewer_capex -> water_monthly.capacity
  water_monthly.capacity -> water_monthly.load_ratio
### migration_monthly
Household arrivals and departures, net migration, population.
Columns:
  - run_id: Owning simulation run.
  - tick: Simulated month.
  - arrivals: People arriving.
  - departures: People leaving.
  - net: arrivals − departures.
  - population: Population after migration.
Derived from: citizen_monthly
  citizen_monthly.satisfaction -> migration_monthly.net

### Glossary
  - Building condition: Visible state band: new, worn, or derelict.
  - Citizen satisfaction: 0–1 well-being of a resident; drives migration.
  - Commute: Home-to-work travel along the road network.
  - Congestion: Traffic load relative to wear-adjusted capacity (0–1).
  - Disposable income: Monthly income remaining after tax and utility/transit bills.
  - Electricity tariff: Retail price charged per kilowatt-hour.
  - Income tax rate: Municipal fraction levied on household gross income.
  - Income tax revenue: Tax collected from household incomes in a month.
  - Migration: Households arriving or leaving in response to city conditions.
  - Municipal budget: City revenue, expenditure, balance, debt, and treasury.
  - Power contract mode: Procurement mode: spot, fixed, or hedged.
  - Power outage fraction: Share of electrical demand left unserved.
  - Property tax rate: Annual fraction of building assessed value collected as tax.
  - Road maintenance budget: Annual spend allocated to road repair.
  - Road wear: Pavement degradation on a network segment (0–1).
  - Tile zoning: Land-use designation controlling what may be built.
  - Transit fare: Price charged per transit ride.
  - Water and sewer capex: Annual capital investment in water and sewer capacity.
  - Water load ratio: Water/sewer demand divided by capacity.
  - Zoning release: Share of undeveloped land opened for development.
